admission.justification: Three concrete design alternatives (in-place v2 schema change, transient clear without persistence, and unguarded MCP auto-suppression) were explicitly weighed and rejected under BUG-R60@v1, and the chosen sibling-sidecar and causal-guard architecture constrains all future provider-limit readers, writers, and CLI tools.

alternatives.option: Store per-window recordedAt timestamps and window-scoped (reportId, windowId, resetsAt) suppressions until resetsAt in sibling sidecar provider-limit-suppressions.json written atomically under provider-limits.lock, keeping provider-limits.json strictly ar-provider-limits/v1 and gating automatic MCP tool-call suppression on a complete host-activity.json in-turn/permission entry with eventAt > recordedAt.
alternatives.reason: Preserves mixed-version ar-provider-limits/v1 Python reader compatibility without schema breakage, prevents five-minute usage re-reads from re-imposing a falsely reported window before resetsAt, and ensures an in-flight pre-limit turn cannot falsely suppress a real limit.

alternatives.option: Embed recordedAt and suppression entries directly inside provider-limits.json or bump provider-limits.json to a v2 schema.
alternatives.reason: The Python reader (observer/provider_limits.py) validates provider-limits.json strictly against ar-provider-limits/v1 with extra=forbid and falls back to EMPTY_PROVIDER_LIMITS on ValidationError, so adding fields or bumping the schema in place would break mixed-version Python readers, running daemons, or older checkouts.
alternatives.reconsider_when: All active Python readers of provider-limits.json drop extra=forbid or migrate together under a coordinated schema-version bump that no longer requires mixed-version v1 coexistence.

alternatives.option: Clear a falsely reported limit once in memory or only until the next five-minute usage recheck instead of persisting a window-scoped suppression until resetsAt.
alternatives.reason: Because the host usage report continues returning the stale exhausted window until its resetsAt passes, a transient clear would be undone on the very next periodic recheck or turn end.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Host usage endpoints stop re-reporting stale exhausted windows once the provider resets the window, so repeated usage reads no longer re-impose a false hold.

alternatives.option: Auto-suppress active provider limits on any bound MCP tool call without requiring causal host-activity.json turn-start evidence (eventAt > recordedAt).
alternatives.reason: A turn that started before the limit was recorded can still execute MCP tool calls before ending; suppressing without strict post-limit turn-start proof would mask genuine limits.
alternatives.reconsider_when: MCP tool calls can no longer execute within turns started prior to limit recording, or the host exposes a stronger causal proof of post-limit turn admission than host-activity.json.

consequences: provider-limits.json remains strictly ar-provider-limits/v1 while serving.paseo.provider_limits owns atomic paired writes with provider-limit-suppressions.json under provider-limits.lock.
Every limit write projects exhausted windows through project_reports_with_suppressions, recomputing until on partial suppression or dropping the report with clearedSeats when none remain.

Automatic suppression from MCP tool calls fails closed unless explicit sidecar recordedAt and complete host-activity.json in-turn/permission state prove eventAt > recordedAt; operators can still override live windows explicitly via agents-remember provider-limits.
context: When a provider usage endpoint falsely reports an exhausted window after reset, Paseo usage re-reads repeatedly re-impose the rate-limit hold even while seats are actively executing turns; meanwhile the Python reader (observer/provider_limits.py) validates provider-limits.json strictly against ar-provider-limits/v1 with extra=forbid and falls back to EMPTY_PROVIDER_LIMITS on ValidationError (while the TypeScript plugin reader ignores unknown keys).
decider: Developer D1054 and D1062 (with Agent Council #2 review D1060) approving BUG-R60@v1
